summary: @servicetitan/datetime-utils preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (numeric-id identifiers, string-array indirection) and, at install time, probes for a local `bun` binary; if absent, it downloads a pinned Bun release archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the `bun` executable to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line module with a large constant string/number array and a rotation function (`WV8StW` shifting a ~1000-entry table) — the classic string-array-rotation obfuscation shape. math_init.js is not referenced by the library's declared `main` (dist/index.js, which contains plain Intl.DateTimeFormat wrappers) and is reached only through the preinstall dropper. The advertised purpose (date/time formatting utilities) has no legitimate need for a separately downloaded language runtime or a 727KB obfuscated module. The net effect on `npm install` is automatic execution of opaque bundled code under a freshly downloaded alien runtime, bypassing Node-based inspection of the install-time code path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
